content.text: Muscle protein synthesis requires two things: resistance training stimulus and an adequate supply of dietary protein. Research suggests consuming 1.6–2.2g of protein per kg of bodyweight daily to maximize muscle growth.

Consume 30–40g of fast-absorbing protein (whey is ideal) within 60–90 minutes of training. Pair with 50–70g of carbohydrates to replenish glycogen stores and spike insulin for nutrient delivery to muscles.

items.question: How many meals should I eat to build muscle?
items.answer: Spread protein intake across 4–5 meals per day, with 30–40g per meal. This maximizes muscle protein synthesis, which has a ceiling per meal of roughly 40g in most people.

items.question: Do I need supplements to build muscle?
items.answer: No, but protein powder is a convenient tool to hit daily protein targets. Creatine monohydrate is the most well-researched supplement for increasing muscle strength and size — 3–5g daily is effective.
